samples.summary: The new `markDirty` call in `applyListLevelChanges` (stale layout for un-selected children) has no test — every list-level test asserts only model `listLevel`, so the fix can regress silently
samples.evidence: The delta adds `markDirty(cellInfo?.tableBlockId ?? change.block.id)` in editor.ts:1604-1610 specifically because a child outside the selection was never marked dirty and "repaints at its old depth". The only tests touching this path are in packages/docs/test/view/editor-tab-bullet.test.ts: 'toolbar indent / outdent carry the subtree as well' (line 329) and 'a header list carries its children too' (line 345), plus editor-on-cursor-move.test.ts:225. All of them assert only `block.listLevel` / callback values read from the document model — they pass identically with the `markDirty` line removed, since the model write happens either way. Nothing asserts that the child block's cached layout lines were recomputed (the repo does have the tooling for this: incremental-layout.test.ts compares `lines` identity, and cursor-move-no-relayout.test.ts counts `measureText` calls through an OffscreenCanvas stub). So the user-visible symptom the fix targets — a nested bullet painted at its old indent after a toolbar Indent/Outdent — is untested and can ship again undetected.

verdict.reason: The `markDirty` call in `editor.ts:1605-1610` (added so a child outside the selection does not repaint at its old list depth) has no test that would fail if it were removed. I enumerated every caller of the affected API repo-wide (`.indent()`/`.outdent()`, excluding node_modules): only editor-tab-bullet.test.ts:337/340/371/374, editor-on-cursor-move.test.ts:234/238, and text-box-editor.test.ts:578-580 (a different implementation). All of them assert only model state (`block.listLevel`, `getBlockType().listLevel`, committed blocks) — none observes layout. The keyboard `Tab` path used by editor-tab-bullet.test.ts:89-95 routes through TextEditor.handleTab (text-editor.ts:2702-2704), whose own applyListLevelChanges (text-editor.ts:2712-2723) has no markDirty because it calls `invalidateLayout()`, so those tests cannot exercise the editor.ts dirty path at all. The behavior is only observable through the layout cache (layout.ts:456-459 and 535-536 reuse `lines`, into which list depth is baked at layout.ts:493-502/543-546), and EditorAPI exposes no layout hook (only _setSelectionForTest/_setEditContextForTest/_getCursorForTest at editor.ts:416-429). Existing tooling that could catch it is never aimed at indent: incremental-layout.test.ts:24-57 tests computeLayout with hand-built dirty Sets (blind to the editor's markDirty); grep of `markDirty|invalidateLayout` across packages/docs/test returns nothing; paint-layout/render-list-marker/cursor-move-no-relayout never touch indent; there are no colocated src tests. Impact if the untested logic regresses is a user-visible stale render of nested bullets after toolbar Indent/Outdent, so major under this lens.

searchedFor: Grep siblingsOf across repo (only src/view/editor.ts, src/view/text-editor.ts)
finding.summary: New table-cell sibling resolution (`siblingsOf`, and `fn(cellBlock, cell.blocks)`) has no test at all
finding.evidence: The diff adds `siblingsOf()` in both editor.ts (~line 1614) and text-editor.ts (~line 2862), plus passes `cell.blocks` from the cell-range, same-cell and table-walk branches of `forEachBlockInSelection`. Subtree detection is entirely driven by which array is handed in, so a wrong array silently re-levels the wrong blocks (e.g. cursor in a cell but siblings resolved to top-level blocks). Nothing exercises it: the new specs in test/view/editor-tab-bullet.test.ts use only flat top-level list items (no `table`/`tableData` fixture anywhere in that file), the new unit test test/model/list-level.test.ts feeds synthetic arrays directly and never goes through the editor, and grep for `siblingsOf` matches only the two src files — no test references it. No test in packages/docs/test indents a list nested inside a table cell.

verdict.reason: The cell-based sibling resolution really is untested. editor.ts:1618-1627 (`siblingsOf`) and the three cell branches that pass `cell.blocks` (editor.ts:1656,1678,1697; text-editor.ts:2844,2856,2863-2873) are only reachable through the six list-level handlers, and every test that invokes those handlers uses flat top-level or header blocks: editor-tab-bullet.test.ts (Tab/indent/outdent, no tableData anywhere, header case at :345-365 only), editor-on-cursor-move.test.ts:234-238, and text-box-editor.test.ts:327-337/578-580 (text boxes have no cells; :334-335 is a bare not.toThrow smoke check). The only Tab-in-a-cell test, header-table-nav.test.ts:196-206, exercises cell *navigation* (Tab appends a row), never a level change, and no Cmd+]/Cmd+[ test exists in the repo at all. test/model/list-level.test.ts, including its "separate sibling arrays" case at :104-116, feeds hand-built arrays straight into planListLevelChanges and never touches blockParentMap/tableData, so it cannot catch a wrong array being resolved for a cell. Since planListLevelChanges (model/list-level.ts:97) derives the subtree purely from the array handed to it, a mis-resolved array would silently re-level the wrong run of blocks in the user's document with no failing test — a data-affecting user path (indent a bullet inside a table cell) left entirely uncovered.
